Wrong: Tryptophan is the dietary precursor for serotonin, melatonin, and niacin, not thyroxin.
Wrong: Taurine is an organic amino sulfonic acid involved in bile salt conjugation.
Wrong: Tryptamine is a decarboxylated amine derived from tryptophan.
questions.explanation: Thyroid follicular cells utilize the aromatic amino acid tyrosine to synthesize the thyroid hormones thyroxin (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3) following specialized iodination.

questions.text: Primary structure of proteins is determined by:
optionReasons: Correct: Primary structure represents the linear amino acid sequence joined exclusively by covalent peptide bonds.
Wrong: Hydrogen bonds stabilize the secondary structure motifs (alpha-helices and beta-sheets).
Wrong: Disulfide bonds participate in tertiary and quaternary protein structure stabilization.
Wrong: Electrostatic interactions participate in holding together tertiary three-dimensional shapes.
Wrong: Hydrophobic effects drive the folding into tertiary structural conformations.
questions.explanation: The primary structure of a protein is its unique linear sequence of amino acids linked together by covalent, amide-type peptide bonds between the alpha-carboxyl group of one residue and the alpha-amino group of the next.

questions.text: Secondary structure of proteins is determined by:
optionReasons: Wrong: Peptide bonds construct the covalent primary backbone, not the secondary folding patterns.
Correct: The folding of a polypeptide chain into local structures like alpha-helices or beta-pleated sheets is stabilized by hydrogen bonds between peptide backbone atoms.
Wrong: Disulfide bridges stabilize higher-order tertiary and quaternary architecture.
Wrong: Electrostatic ionic bonds contribute primarily to tertiary conformation dynamics.
Wrong: Hydrophobic core collapse stabilizes tertiary packaging.
questions.explanation: Secondary protein structures are maintained by hydrogen bonding interactions between the carbonyl oxygen (-C=O) and amide hydrogen (-N-H) atoms comprising the peptide bond backbone.

questions.text: Isoelectric pH is the pH at which:
options: Protein molecule carries no net charges.
The disulfide bonds in protein molecule are disrupted.
optionReasons: Wrong: Isoelectric point does not imply structural denaturation, which involves unfolding.
Correct: The isoelectric point (pI) is defined specifically as the precise pH value at which a zwitterionic molecule carries an equal balance of charges, meaning its net electrical charge is zero.
Wrong: Proteins exhibit their lowest solubility at their isoelectric point, often aggregating and precipitating.
Wrong: Disulfide bond integrity depends on redox status, not directly on the isoelectric pH configuration.
questions.explanation: At the isoelectric pH (pI), the total positive charges on the protein's functional groups perfectly equal the negative charges, rendering the molecule electrochemically neutral and immobile in an electric field.

questions.text: The protein bond that is NOT lost by denaturation is:
optionReasons: Correct: Denaturation alters the spatial conformation of proteins by breaking non-covalent interactions, but it leaves the covalent primary peptide bonds completely intact.
Wrong: Hydrogen bonds are highly susceptible to denaturation by thermal or chemical agents.
Wrong: Strong denaturants and reducing agents routinely disrupt stabilizing disulfide bridges.
Wrong: Electrostatic ionic bonds are sensitive to pH changes and salt concentrations during denaturation.
Wrong: Hydrophobic core packing is disrupted by detergents or organic solvents during denaturation.
questions.explanation: Denaturation alters secondary, tertiary, and quaternary conformations without cleaving the covalent peptide backbone bonds. Therefore, the primary amino acid sequence remains intact.

questions.text: Tertiary structure of proteins is determined by:
optionReasons: Wrong: Hydrogen bonds contribute, but they are not the sole stabilizing force for tertiary conformation.
Wrong: Disulfide bridges provide covalent reinforcement, but they operate alongside other interactions.
Wrong: Electrostatic ionic interactions (salt bridges) are important, but not exclusively.
Wrong: Hydrophobic interactions drive folding, but all other listed forces stabilize the final structure.

Correct: The three-dimensional tertiary folding of a polypeptide is stabilized by a combination of hydrogen bonds, disulfide bonds, electrostatic interactions, and hydrophobic forces between side chains.
questions.explanation: Tertiary protein structure refers to the overall 3D conformation of a single polypeptide chain, stabilized by interactions between amino acid R-side chains, encompassing both non-covalent forces and covalent disulfide links.

questions.text: The zwitter ion is:
optionReasons: Correct: A zwitterion (or dipolar ion) contains distinct positively and negatively charged chemical groups, yielding a net charge of zero.
Wrong: Purely positively charged ions are called cations.
Wrong: Purely negatively charged ions are called anions.
Wrong: Zwitterions do contain localized charges, unlike completely non-charged neutral molecular species.
questions.explanation: Amino acids in aqueous solution at physiological pH exist as zwitterions, featuring a protonated amino group (-NH3+) and a deprotonated carboxyl group (-COO-).

questions.text: All the following amino acids enter in the structure of proteins EXCEPT:
optionReasons: Wrong: Glycine is a standard proteinogenic amino acid encoded by codons.
Correct: Homoserine is a non-proteinogenic amino acid that functions as an intermediate in methionine/threonine metabolism, lacking a cognate tRNA.
Wrong: Phenylalanine is a standard proteinogenic aromatic amino acid.
Wrong: Alanine is a standard proteinogenic aliphatic amino acid used heavily in protein synthesis.
questions.explanation: Homoserine is a metabolic pathway intermediate rather than a proteinogenic amino acid, meaning it is not incorporated into proteins during ribosomal translation.

questions.text: Glycine is characterized by:
optionReasons: Wrong: It is optically inactive, but this represents only one of its correct features.
Wrong: It lacks a chiral asymmetric carbon, but the other choices are also correct.
Wrong: It is the smallest possible amino acid (R group is H), but this is not the only true statement.
Wrong: It behaves as a non-polar aliphatic amino acid structurally, but other features apply.
Correct: Every statement perfectly defines glycine's unique structural and stereochemical properties.
questions.explanation: Glycine has a single hydrogen atom as its side chain (R = H). This makes its alpha-carbon symmetric, rendering it the smallest, non-polar, and optically inactive proteinogenic amino acid.

questions.text: Ornithin is:
optionReasons: Correct: Ornithine contains an extra amino group in its aliphatic side chain, classifying it chemically as a basic amino acid.
Wrong: Ornithine is synthesized inside human cells during the urea cycle, making it non-essential.
Wrong: Ornithine is a non-proteinogenic intermediate that is not post-translationally or ribosomally incorporated into protein polymers.
Wrong: Since it is not essential and absent from protein structure, 'All of these' is incorrect.
questions.explanation: Ornithine plays a critical catalytic role within the hepatic urea cycle, operating as a basic amino acid intermediate generated from arginine via the arginase enzyme.

questions.text: The only amino acid that is ketogenic but NOT glycogenic is:
optionReasons: Wrong: Isoleucine is both glucogenic and ketogenic.
Wrong: Tyrosine is an aromatic amino acid that is both glucogenic and ketogenic.
Correct: Leucine (along with lysine) is strictly ketogenic, but given the specific phrasing and options, leucine is classic.
Wrong: Phenylalanine is amphibolic, breaking down into both glucogenic and ketogenic fragments.
Wrong: Lysine is also strictly ketogenic, but Leucine is typically classified as the classic model amino acid for pure ketogenesis.
questions.explanation: Leucine and Lysine are the only two purely ketogenic amino acids. Their catabolic pathways form acetyl-CoA and acetoacetate, making them incapable of serving as substrates for net glucose synthesis via gluconeogenesis.

questions.text: A sulfur containing amino acid that is NOT found in proteins is:
optionReasons: Wrong: Homoserine is a non-protein amino acid, but it contains a hydroxyl group, not sulfur.
Correct: Homocysteine contains a sulfhydryl (-SH) group but is a metabolic intermediate not incorporated into structural proteins.
Wrong: Methionine is a sulfur-containing amino acid regularly incorporated into proteins.
Wrong: Cysteine is a structural sulfur-containing proteinogenic amino acid.
Wrong: Threonine contains a hydroxyl functional group, not a sulfur atom.
questions.explanation: Homocysteine is a sulfur-bearing homologue of cysteine. It functions within the methionine metabolic cycle but lacks a genetic codon or tRNA for entry into structural proteins.

questions.text: Methionine and threonine are:
optionReasons: Wrong: Tyrosine is the primary phenol-containing amino acid.
Wrong: Basic amino acids comprise lysine, arginine, and histidine.
Wrong: Acidic amino acids are glutamate and aspartate.
Wrong: Both must be acquired from dietary sources, meaning they are essential.
Correct: Methionine and threonine are both classified as nutritionally essential amino acids for human metabolic needs.
questions.explanation: Humans lack the complex enzymatic multi-step machinery needed to synthesize the hydrocarbon carbon skeletons of methionine and threonine, requiring dietary intake.

questions.text: All of the following about protein denaturation is true EXCEPT:
options: It is loss of primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary structures.
It causes loss of biological activity of proteins.
Strong acids can cause protein Denaturation
optionReasons: Correct: Denaturation does not affect the primary structure, as covalent peptide bonds remain completely unbroken.
Wrong: This statement is true; unfolding disrupts active conformations and eliminates biological function.
Wrong: This statement is true; exposure of hydrophobic interiors causes aggregation and precipitation.
Wrong: This statement is true; strong acids disturb ionic states and hydrogen bonds, driving denaturation.
questions.explanation: Protein denaturation involves the structural unfolding of higher-order confirmations (secondary, tertiary, quaternary) while leaving the primary amino acid sequence intact.

questions.text: Cysteine, cystine and methionine are:
optionReasons: Wrong: Cysteine and cystine are non-essential, as they can be synthesized from methionine.
Wrong: Cysteine and methionine are standard proteinogenic blocks.
Wrong: Acidic amino acids possess extra carboxyl groups, unlike these sulfur-bearing variants.
Correct: Cysteine, cystine (di-cysteine), and methionine all contain sulfur atoms within their chemical structures.
questions.explanation: These amino acids share the common structural characteristic of containing sulfur: methionine features a thioether link, while cysteine and cystine contain sulfhydryl and disulfide functional groups.

questions.text: elastin is:
optionReasons: Correct: Elastin is a scleroprotein (fibrous structural protein) found in connective tissues, characterized by its elasticity and insolubility.
Wrong: Chromoproteins are conjugated proteins bound to pigmented groups like heme.
Wrong: Metalloproteins contain bound functional metal ions.
Wrong: Phosphoproteins are conjugated with phosphoric acid residues.
Wrong: Glycoproteins contain covalently linked oligosaccharide carbohydrate chains.
questions.explanation: Scleroproteins, or fibrous proteins, include insoluble structural tissue components like collagen, keratin, and elastin, which provide mechanical support.

questions.text: Collagen is:
optionReasons: Wrong: It is insoluble, but this represents only one of several accurate properties listed.
Wrong: Thermal denaturing via boiling transforms it into gelatin, but other options are also correct.
Wrong: It is rich in glycine, but the other choices are also true.
Wrong: It forms a firm triple-helical structure, but this is not the only true statement.
Correct: Every single option lists an established physical, chemical, or structural trait of collagen molecules.
questions.explanation: Collagen is an insoluble fibrous protein with high tensile strength, characterized by a high glycine content. Thermal denaturation via boiling unfolds its structure into soluble gelatin.

questions.text: Arginine and lysine are present in excess in:
optionReasons: Correct: Histones are basic proteins that contain large amounts of positive arginine and lysine residues to bind negatively charged DNA.
Wrong: Albumin is a neutral/slightly acidic plasma protein.
Wrong: Gliadins are plant proline-and-glutamine-rich prolamins.
Wrong: Globulins do not contain excess basic amino acids.
Wrong: Only histones feature an excess of basic amino acids.
Wrong: One specific valid option is present.
questions.explanation: Histones require a net positive charge at physiological pH to interact electrostatically with the negatively charged phosphate backbone of DNA, achieved via high arginine and lysine content.

questions.text: Aspartic acid and glutamic acid are:
optionReasons: Wrong: Both are non-essential amino acids synthesized from tricarboxylic acid cycle intermediates.
Correct: Aspartic acid and glutamic acid contain a second carboxyl group (-COOH) in their side chains, classifying them as acidic amino acids.
Wrong: Basic proteins are rich in positive residues like lysine and arginine.
Wrong: Collagen is characterized by high levels of glycine, proline, and hydroxyproline.
questions.explanation: Aspartate and glutamate possess carboxylated side chains that carry a net negative charge at physiological pH, classifying them as acidic amino acids.

questions.text: An amino acid containing guanidine group is:
optionReasons: Wrong: Leucine has a branched hydrocarbon aliphatic chain.
Correct: Arginine's basic side chain terminates in a planar guanidino group, which stays protonated across physiological conditions.
Wrong: Citrulline features a ureido group, not a guanidino group.
Wrong: Isoleucine contains a branched aliphatic secondary butyl side chain.
Wrong: Lysine possesses an epsilon-amino group on its aliphatic side chain.
questions.explanation: Arginine contains a guanidino functional group (-NH-C(NH)=NH2+) that gives it a high pKa value (~12.5), making it strongly basic.

questions.text: Ceruloplasmin is:
optionReasons: Wrong: Chromoproteins emphasize light absorption via pigment linkages.
Correct: Ceruloplasmin is a classic metalloprotein, serving as the major copper-carrying protein in blood plasma.
Wrong: It does not utilize structural phosphate ester modifications.
Wrong: While it is glycosylated, its primary biochemical classification is based on its functional copper-metalloprotein status.
questions.explanation: Ceruloplasmin binds six copper atoms per molecule, carrying over 95% of total serum copper while functioning as an enzyme with ferroxidase activity.

questions.text: Which of the following is a globular protein:
optionReasons: Wrong: Albumin is globular, but Myoglobin is the designated answer from original keys.
Wrong: Globulins are globular, but Myoglobin is a distinct globular protein choice.
Wrong: Collagen is a classic structural fibrous protein.
Correct: Myoglobin is a classic model for monomeric, water-soluble globular proteins with a compact spherical architecture.
questions.explanation: Myoglobin is a compact, globular hemoprotein found in muscle tissue, serving as a classic model for studying protein folding and three-dimensional structural architecture.

questions.text: A heterocyclic amino acid is:
optionReasons: Correct: Tryptophan contains an indole ring system, which is a heterocyclic structure containing nitrogen.
Wrong: Phenylalanine contains a homocyclic benzene ring system.
Wrong: Tyrosine contains a homocyclic phenolic ring system.
Wrong: Lysine has a flexible acyclic, aliphatic straight-chain structure.
Wrong: Isoleucine is a branched-chain acyclic aliphatic amino acid.
questions.explanation: Heterocyclic amino acids feature a cyclic ring containing atoms from at least two different elements. Tryptophan's indole ring consists of a benzene ring fused to a nitrogen-containing pyrrole ring.

questions.text: The amphoteric property of amino acids is due to the presence of:
optionReasons: Wrong: The amino group acts as a base but cannot provide dual amphoteric properties alone.
Wrong: The carboxyl group acts as an acid but cannot provide dual amphoteric properties alone.
Correct: Amphoterism means acting as both an acid and a base, enabled by the basic amino group (-NH2) and acidic carboxyl group (-COOH).
Wrong: The indole ring is a neutral heterocyclic structure, not an amphoteric buffer.
Wrong: The phenyl ring is a hydrophobic aromatic group with no acid-base buffering properties.
questions.explanation: Amino acids are amphoteric because they possess both basic amino groups (proton acceptors) and acidic carboxyl groups (proton donors), allowing them to act as zwitterionic buffers.

questions.text: Leucine is:
optionReasons: Wrong: Leucine has a neutral, hydrophobic branched aliphatic side chain.
Correct: Leucine catabolism yields only acetyl-CoA and acetoacetate, making it a strictly ketogenic amino acid.
Wrong: Leucine is an essential branched-chain amino acid that humans must obtain from diet.
Wrong: Leucine is an acyclic branched aliphatic molecule, lacking rings.
Wrong: Leucine is a branched-chain amino acid alongside valine and isoleucine.
questions.explanation: Leucine is one of the two strictly ketogenic proteinogenic amino acids. Its breakdown products cannot feed net gluconeogenesis pathways.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements about the major collagen type from skin or bone is INCORRECT:
options: One third of the amino acids of collagen is glycine.
Ascorbic acid is required for the synthesis of collagen.
The collagen molecule contains nonhelical chains.
Collagen molecule is trimmer composed of three monomers, each containing approximately 1050 amino acids.
By boiling, collagen molecule gives gelatin.
optionReasons: Wrong: This statement is correct; glycine comprises one third of collagen's primary sequence.
Wrong: This statement is correct; vitamin C is an essential cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases.
Correct: The core collagen molecule is composed of tightly wrapped helical alpha-chains, making the claim that it contains 'nonhelical chains' structurally false.
Wrong: This statement is correct; collagen is a triple-helical trimer of long polypeptide monomers.
Wrong: This statement is correct; boiling denatures the triple helix into soluble gelatin strands.
questions.explanation: Collagen is composed of three left-handed alpha-chains wrapped into a right-handed triple helix. It does not contain structural nonhelical chains in its mature core.

questions.text: Albumin, globulin, histones and scleroproteins belong to the class of:
optionReasons: Correct: Simple proteins yield exclusively free amino acids upon complete chemical hydrolysis, without producing non-protein prosthetic groups.
Wrong: Conjugated proteins contain a non-amino acid prosthetic group, such as lipids or carbohydrates.
Wrong: Derived proteins are degradation products or denatured forms of natural proteins.
Wrong: While histones are basic, albumin is slightly acidic; they do not all share basic properties.
Wrong: Scleroproteins and histones do not belong to the acidic protein class.
questions.explanation: Proteins are classified as simple when their composition consists solely of amino acids. Examples include albumins, globulins, histones, and structural scleroproteins.

questions.text: All of the following are sulfur containing amino acids EXCEPT:
optionReasons: Wrong: Cysteine is a standard sulfur-containing amino acid with a thiol group.
Wrong: Homocysteine is a sulfur-containing pathway intermediate.
Wrong: Cystine is a sulfur-containing disulfide-bonded dimer of two cysteines.
Wrong: Methionine is an essential sulfur-containing amino acid containing a thioether group.
Correct: Threonine is a hydroxylated aliphatic amino acid (-OH) that contains no sulfur.
questions.explanation: Threonine contains a secondary hydroxyl group (-OH) on its side chain, whereas cysteine, homocysteine, cystine, and methionine all contain sulfur atoms.

questions.text: Methionine is:
optionReasons: Wrong: Acidic amino acids contain extra carboxyl groups, which methionine lacks.
Wrong: Basic amino acids contain nitrogenous basic side chains, unlike methionine.
Correct: Methionine features a non-polar thioether group (-S-CH3) within its aliphatic side chain, classifying it as a sulfur-containing amino acid.
Wrong: Hydroxyl amino acids contain -OH groups, such as serine and threonine.
Wrong: Aromatic amino acids contain ring systems, like phenylalanine or tyrosine.
questions.explanation: Methionine is an essential aliphatic amino acid characterized by a hydrophobic sulfur-containing thioether side chain.

questions.text: Lysine is:
optionReasons: Wrong: Neutral amino acids carry no net charge on their side chain at physiological pH.
Wrong: Acidic amino acids carry a negative charge from side-chain carboxyl groups.
Correct: Lysine contains an epsilon-amino group on its aliphatic side chain, which carries a positive charge at physiological pH, making it a basic amino acid.
Wrong: Heterocyclic amino acids contain ring heteroatoms, unlike the straight chain of lysine.
Wrong: Aromatic amino acids possess ring systems, which lysine lacks.
questions.explanation: Lysine is a basic amino acid with a positively charged side-chain amino group (-NH3+) at physiological pH.

questions.text: Collagen is rich in:
optionReasons: Correct: Collagen is characterized by a repeating Gly-X-Y motif, where X is typically proline and Y is hydroxyproline.
Wrong: Collagen does not contain high amounts of acidic glutamate.
Wrong: Collagen is notably poor in sulfur-containing cysteine and cystine residues.
Wrong: Hydrophobic branched-chain amino acids are not major structural features of collagen.
questions.explanation: Glycine makes up one-third of collagen's sequence, while proline and hydroxyproline provide the structural rigidity required to stabilize its triple helix.

questions.text: A vasodilator substance is produce by a decarboxylation of:
optionReasons: Wrong: Methionine decarboxylation participates in polyamine synthesis pathways, not direct vasodilation.
Correct: Enzymatic decarboxylation of the amino acid histidine removes its carboxyl group to generate histamine, a powerful vasodilator.
Wrong: Decarboxylation of glutamate yields GABA, an inhibitory central nervous system neurotransmitter.
Wrong: Threonine catabolism does not yield a vasoactive amine.
Wrong: Phenylalanine pathways yield catecholamines, which typically act as vasoconstrictors rather than primary vasodilators.
questions.explanation: Histidine undergoes decarboxylation catalyzed by histidine decarboxylase to produce histamine, a biogenic amine that triggers vasodilation and vascular permeability.

questions.text: Decarboxylation of tryptophan produces:
optionReasons: Wrong: Serotonin synthesis requires both hydroxylation and decarboxylation steps, not simple direct decarboxylation.
Wrong: Tyramine is produced by the decarboxylation of tyrosine.
Correct: Direct decarboxylation of free tryptophan removes its carboxyl group, producing the biogenic amine tryptamine.
Wrong: Tyrosine is formed by the hydroxylation of phenylalanine, not the decarboxylation of tryptophan.
questions.explanation: Direct decarboxylation of free tryptophan by aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase produces tryptamine, a monoamine alkaloid.

questions.text: All of the following are hydroxy (OH) containing amino acids EXCEPT:
optionReasons: Wrong: Serine contains a primary hydroxyl group (-CH2OH).
Wrong: Homoserine is a non-proteinogenic amino acid containing a terminal hydroxyl group.
Wrong: Threonine contains a secondary hydroxyl group.
Correct: Glycine's side chain is a single hydrogen atom (-H), meaning it contains no hydroxyl group.
questions.explanation: Serine, threonine, and homoserine are aliphatic hydroxy amino acids. Glycine is the simplest amino acid and contains only a hydrogen atom as its side chain.

questions.text: Which of the following amino acid groups contains ONLY nonessential amino acids:
optionReasons: Wrong: This group includes methionine, which is an essential amino acid.
Wrong: This group includes lysine and histidine, which are essential amino acids.
Wrong: This group includes phenylalanine and tryptophan, which are essential amino acids.
Correct: The acidic amino acids, aspartate and glutamate, can both be synthesized in the human body from citric acid cycle intermediates.
questions.explanation: Aspartate and glutamate are synthesized via transamination of oxaloacetate and alpha-ketoglutarate, making the acidic amino acid group entirely nonessential.

questions.text: An amino acids present in natural proteins is:
optionReasons: Wrong: Ornithine is a urea cycle intermediate and is not incorporated into proteins.
Wrong: beta-Alanine is found in pantothenic acid but is not a proteinogenic amino acid.
Wrong: Citrulline is a metabolic intermediate and is not used in ribosomal protein synthesis.
Wrong: Homoserine is an intermediate in amino acid metabolism and is absent from proteins.
Correct: Valine is a standard proteinogenic amino acid encoded by the universal genetic code for protein assembly.
questions.explanation: Valine is one of the 20 standard amino acids used by ribosomes to build proteins, whereas the other options serve exclusively as metabolic intermediates.

questions.text: A phosphprotein is:
optionReasons: Correct: Casein, the primary protein in milk, is a classic phosphoprotein with phosphate groups esterified to serine residues.
Wrong: Albumin is a simple plasma protein, not a conjugated phosphoprotein.
Wrong: Globulins are simple spherical plasma proteins without structural phosphorylation.
Wrong: Histones are basic structural DNA-binding proteins, not classified as phosphoproteins.
questions.explanation: Phosphoproteins are conjugated proteins where phosphoric acid is chemically bonded to hydroxy amino acids like serine or threonine. Casein is a classic example.

questions.text: A basic protein associated with nucleic acids is:
optionReasons: Wrong: Actin is a structural microfilament cytoskeletal protein, not a basic nuclear protein.
Wrong: Myosin is a motor protein involved in muscle contraction.
Correct: Histones are basic proteins rich in arginine and lysine that bind to the negatively charged phosphate backbone of DNA.
Wrong: Collagen is an extracellular structural fibrous protein.
questions.explanation: Histones are basic proteins found in eukaryotic cell nuclei that package and order DNA into structural units called nucleosomes.

questions.text: A protein that contains 33% glycine amino acid is:
optionReasons: Wrong: Albumin contains a typical globular distribution of amino acids with low glycine content.
Wrong: Globulins do not have a repetitive glycine backbone architecture.
Correct: Elastin contains approximately 33% glycine residues throughout its structure, though it lacks collagen's repeating triple helix.
Wrong: Casein is an amorphous phosphoprotein with lower glycine levels.
Wrong: Histones are characterized by high levels of lysine and arginine rather than glycine.
questions.explanation: Like collagen, elastin is structurally composed of about one-third glycine residues, which allow for the formation of its characteristic cross-linked random-coil structure.

questions.text: An imino group is present in structure of:
optionReasons: Correct: Proline contains a secondary amino group integrated into a five-membered pyrrolidine ring, classifying it as an imino acid.
Wrong: Alanine contains a standard primary alpha-amino group.
Wrong: Serine possesses a primary alpha-amino group alongside its hydroxyl side chain.
Wrong: Aspartic acid contains a standard primary alpha-amino group and two carboxyl groups.
questions.explanation: Proline is technically an imino acid because its side chain cyclizes back onto its own alpha-amino nitrogen atom, forming a secondary amine structure.

questions.text: Elastin is cross-linked through its:
optionReasons: Wrong: Glutamate side chains form ionic links, not the covalent desmosine units of elastin.
Wrong: Glutamine side chains are not involved in elastin's specialized cross-linking.
Correct: Lysyl oxidase modifies lysine side chains to form allysine condensations, creating the desmosine cross-links unique to elastin.
Wrong: Methionine does not participate in extracellular structural cross-linking.
questions.explanation: Desmosine cross-links are formed by the condensation of three allysine pathways and one unmodified lysine residue, all derived from lysine side chains.

questions.text: Amino acids considered non essential for human are:
optionReasons: Wrong: Both essential and nonessential amino acids are incorporated into proteins.
Correct: Nonessential amino acids are defined as those that the human body can synthesize endogenously, making dietary intake optional.
Wrong: Decarboxylation status does not dictate nutritional essentiality.
Wrong: Transamination capability does not differentiate nutritional essentiality categories.
questions.explanation: Nutritionally nonessential amino acids can be synthesized within the body via metabolic pathways using carbon skeletons from intermediates and amino groups from other sources.

questions.text: Sulfur containing amino acid is:
optionReasons: Wrong: Keratan sulfate is a sulfated glycosaminoglycan carbohydrate polymer, not an amino acid.
Wrong: Chondroitin sulfate is a complex sulfated glycosaminoglycan carbohydrate, not an amino acid.
Correct: Cysteine is a standard proteinogenic amino acid containing a reactive sulfur atom in its sulfhydryl (-SH) group.
Wrong: Homoserine is a hydroxylated metabolic intermediate containing no sulfur.
Wrong: Glutathione contains sulfur, but it is a tripeptide rather than a single amino acid.
questions.explanation: Cysteine is a sulfur-containing amino acid with a thiol group that can form stabilizing disulfide bonds within protein structures.

questions.text: Gelatin is:
optionReasons: Correct: Gelatin is produced by the thermal denaturation and partial hydrolysis of structural collagen fibers.
Wrong: Boiled globulins form insoluble coagulants, not gelatinous mixtures.
Wrong: Elastin does not convert into gelatin upon boiling due to its unique cross-links.
Wrong: Gelatin is a degraded simple protein, not a conjugated protein bound to a prosthetic group.
Wrong: Gelatin is a degradation product of a scleroprotein, not a biosynthetic precursor.
questions.explanation: Boiling collagen breaks down its triple-helical structure, melting the inter-chain hydrogen bonds to yield water-soluble gelatin strands.

questions.text: Desmosine cross-links are present in the structure of:
optionReasons: Wrong: Collagen utilizes aldol condensations and histidino-hydroxylysinonorleucine links, not desmosine.
Correct: Desmosine and isodesmosine cross-links are unique to elastin, providing its characteristic rubber-like elastic properties.
Wrong: Casein is an amorphous phosphoprotein that lacks covalent structural cross-links.
Wrong: Keratin is stabilized by covalent disulfide bonds between cysteine residues, not desmosine.
questions.explanation: Desmosine cross-links are formed by the condensation of four lysine residues, connecting individual elastin chains into a flexible, elastic network.

questions.text: Glutathione is tripeptide formed of:
optionReasons: Wrong: This combination does not form glutathione.
Wrong: Glutathione contains cysteine and glycine, which are missing from this choice.
Wrong: This sequence is incorrect and lacks glutathione's constituent residues.
Wrong: Glutathione contains cysteine, not its oxidized dimer cystine.
Correct: Glutathione is a tripeptide composed of glutamate, cysteine, and glycine (gamma-glutamyl-cysteinyl-glycine).
questions.explanation: Glutathione (GSH) features a unique peptide bond between the gamma-carboxyl group of glutamate and the amino group of cysteine, serving as a cellular antioxidant.

questions.text: The terms 'primary', 'secondary' and 'tertiary' structure in protein chemistry refer to:
options: 'Amino acids sequence', 'hydrophobic, electrostatic, disulfide, hydrogen bonds' and 'alpha-helix' respectively.
'Amino acids sequence', 'alpha-helix', and 'hydrophobic, electrostatic, disulfide, hydrogen bonds' respectively.
optionReasons: Wrong: These terms describe specific secondary conformations, not the full structural hierarchy.
Wrong: This option mixes up the definitions of secondary and tertiary structural forces.
Wrong: These are specific chemical interactions, not the hierarchical structural levels.
Correct: Primary structure is the amino acid sequence; secondary structure includes conformations like the alpha-helix; tertiary structure is stabilized by various side-chain interactions.
questions.explanation: Protein structure is organized hierarchically: primary is the sequence, secondary describes local backbone folding, and tertiary is the overall 3D conformation stabilized by side-chain interactions.

questions.text: The following are basic essential amino acids EXCEPT:
optionReasons: Wrong: Histidine is a basic amino acid with an imidazole side chain, essential for humans.
Wrong: Lysine is a basic essential amino acid with an epsilon-amino group.
Wrong: Arginine is a basic amino acid with a guanidino group, conditionally essential.
Correct: Leucine is an essential amino acid, but it is hydrophobic and branched-chain, not basic.
questions.explanation: Lysine, arginine, and histidine are basic amino acids. Leucine is a non-polar, branched-chain amino acid.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements about the major collagen type from skin or bone is CORRECT:
options: One third of the amino acids of collagen is hydroxyproline.
Ascorbic acid is required for the synthesis of collagen.
The collagen molecule contains nonhelical chains.
Collagen molecule is dimmer composed of two monomers, each containing approximately 1050 amino acids.
The polypeptide chains of collagen are held together by disulfide bonds.
optionReasons: Wrong: Glycine makes up one third of the amino acids in collagen, not hydroxyproline.
Correct: Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) is an essential cofactor for the prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase enzymes involved in collagen synthesis.
Wrong: The core collagen molecule consists of structured helical alpha-chains.
Wrong: Collagen is a trimer composed of three polypeptide chains, not a dimer.
Wrong: The triple-helical chains of interstitial collagen are held together by hydrogen bonds, lacking internal disulfide links.
questions.explanation: Vitamin C maintains the iron cofactor of prolyl hydroxylase in its reduced Fe2+ state, which is necessary for the hydroxylation steps that stabilize collagen's triple helix.

questions.text: The bonds present in the primary structure of proteins are:
optionReasons: Wrong: Hydrogen bonds stabilize secondary structures, not the primary sequence.
Correct: The primary structure of a protein is defined by its linear sequence of amino acids linked by covalent peptide bonds.
Wrong: Disulfide bonds participate in tertiary and quaternary structural stabilization.
Wrong: Electrostatic bonds stabilize higher-order tertiary folding configurations.
Wrong: Only peptide bonds define the primary backbone sequence.
questions.explanation: The primary structure consists of the linear sequence of amino acids held together exclusively by covalent amide peptide bonds.

questions.text: All the following related to collagen is true EXCEPT:
options: Formed of two polypeptide helical chain
optionReasons: Wrong: This statement is true; collagen is the primary protein component of connective tissues.
Wrong: This statement is true; glycine accounts for roughly one-third of its amino acid content.
Wrong: This statement is true; proline and lysine residues undergo post-translational hydroxylation.
Correct: Collagen is a trimer formed of three polypeptide helical chains, making the claim of 'two chains' false.
Wrong: This statement is true; the glycine residues allow for tight, compact packaging of the triple helix.
questions.explanation: Collagen molecules are tropocollagen trimers composed of three left-handed alpha-chains wrapped around a central axis into a tight right-handed triple helix.

questions.text: In proteins, the alpha-helix and beta-pleated sheet are example of:
optionReasons: Wrong: Primary structure refers to the linear sequence of amino acids.
Correct: The alpha-helix and beta-pleated sheet are local folding patterns of the polypeptide backbone, which define secondary structure.
Wrong: Tertiary structure describes the overall three-dimensional folding of a single polypeptide chain.
Wrong: Quaternary structure refers to the spatial arrangement of multiple polypeptide subunits.
questions.explanation: Secondary structures are regular, repeating local folding patterns stabilized by hydrogen bonds between the carbonyl oxygen and amide nitrogen atoms of the peptide backbone.

questions.text: The most abundant structural protein is:
optionReasons: Correct: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the human body, accounting for roughly 25% to 35% of total protein content.
Wrong: Keratin is abundant in epithelial structures but is less prevalent overall than collagen.
Wrong: Fibronectin is an extracellular matrix glycoprotein present in lower amounts.
Wrong: Elastin provides tissue elasticity but is less abundant than collagen.
questions.explanation: Collagen serves as the primary structural element of connective tissues throughout the body, including bone, skin, tendons, and cartilage, making it the most abundant protein in mammals.

questions.text: Which of the following groups consists entirely of amino acids which are nutritionally essential for human:
optionReasons: Wrong: Tyrosine is nonessential because it can be synthesized from phenylalanine.
Wrong: Alanine is a nonessential amino acid synthesized via transamination of pyruvate.
Wrong: Glutamate and cysteine are nonessential amino acids.
Wrong: This group contains nonessential tyrosine.
Correct: Lysine, tryptophan, phenylalanine, and threonine are all essential amino acids that cannot be synthesized by human metabolic pathways.
questions.explanation: The nine fully essential amino acids are histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, and valine.

questions.text: The compound shown beside:
options: Is an intermediate in urea cycle
Is the source of C4, C5 and N7 of purine base.
Releases ammonia (NH3) when converted to alpha-ketoglutarate
optionReasons: Wrong: Glutamate is not a direct intermediate of the cyclic urea pathway.
Wrong: Serine and palmitoyl-CoA serve as the biosynthetic sources of sphingosine base formations.
Wrong: The molecular structure context corresponds to glutamate, not lysine.
Wrong: Glycine provides C4, C5, and N7 atoms during the purine ring construction.
Correct: Glutamate undergoes oxidative deamination catalyzed by glutamate dehydrogenase, releasing free ammonia (NH3) and forming alpha-ketoglutarate.
questions.explanation: Based on the provided options, the compound described is glutamate. Glutamate dehydrogenase catalyzes its conversion to alpha-ketoglutarate, releasing free ammonium ions.

questions.text: For proteins and peptides — indicate True (T) or False (F) for each statement:

statements.text: Glutathione is a physiological active peptide with a free SH group
Dialysis means separation of protein colloids from crystalloids
Denaturation of proteins disturbs primary structure of proteins
Glycoproteins are considered simple proteins
Disulfide and peptide bonds are weak bonds

questions.explanation: Glutathione contains a free sulfhydryl (-SH) group on its cysteine residue, acting as an antioxidant. Dialysis uses a semipermeable membrane to separate large protein colloids from small crystalloid ions. Denaturation alters secondary, tertiary, and quaternary folding but leaves covalent peptide bonds (primary structure) intact. Glycoproteins contain a carbohydrate prosthetic group, making them conjugated proteins. Peptide and disulfide links are strong covalent bonds.

questions.text: For amino acids — indicate True (T) or False (F) for each statement:

statements.text: Tyrosine is an aromatic essential amino acid
An essential sulfur containing amino acid is methionine
Amino acids have high melting points above 200 degrees C
Amino acids share in urea cycle are arginine orinithin and citruline
Arginine is non-essential amino acid

questions.explanation: Tyrosine is an aromatic amino acid but is non-essential because the body synthesizes it from phenylalanine. Methionine is a strictly essential sulfur-containing amino acid. Free amino acids form stable ionic zwitterionic crystal lattices, leading to high melting points over 200 degrees C. Arginine, ornithine, and citrulline are the primary amino acid carriers of the urea cycle. Arginine is classified as semi-essential or conditionally essential.

questions.text: Denaturation of proteins — indicate True (T) or False (F) for each statement:

statements.text: means unfolding and loss of primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure
Denaturated proteins lose their biological activity
Denaturated proteins are easily precipitated
Repeated freezing and thawing do not cause denaturation: cause disruption of hydrogen and other weak bonds
Heavy metals as lead and mercury salts cause denaturation

questions.explanation: Denaturation causes the loss of secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structures, but does not affect the primary sequence. Unfolding destroys the native active conformation, resulting in a loss of biological function and exposing internal hydrophobic groups, which leads to precipitation. Freezing and thawing disrupt stabilizing hydrogen bonds, causing denaturation. Heavy metal ions bind functional side chains, disrupting salt bridges and denaturing the protein.

questions.text: Collagen — indicate True (T) or False (F) for each statement:

statements.text: Collagens form about 30% of total body proteins
Collagen is deficient in glycine
Collagen consist of 3 polypeptide chains called alpha-chains
Denaturation of collagen by heating produces gelatin
Scurvy is a collagen disease resulting from deficiency in ascorbic acid

questions.explanation: Collagen is the most abundant protein in mammals, constituting roughly 30% of total body protein mass. It is highly rich in glycine, which occupies every third position (Gly-X-Y). A tropocollagen unit consists of three left-handed alpha-chains wound into a right-handed triple helix. Thermal denaturation breaks down this triple helix configuration to produce soluble gelatin. Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) is a mandatory cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases; its deficiency causes scurvy.

questions.text: In the figure of polypeptide below (glycine - serine - cystine - glutamate - aspartate - asparagine - methionine - cystine - phenylalanine) — indicate True (T) or False (F) for each statement:

statements.text: Glutamate is an aromatic essential amino acid
The N-terminus is located in glycine residue
Serine is the site of phosphate attachment
Hydroxyproline is synthesized post-translationally
Phenylalanine contains indole ring

questions.explanation: Glutamate is an acidic, non-essential amino acid. By biochemical convention, sequences are read from left to right starting at the amino N-terminus (Glycine) and ending at the carboxyl C-terminus (Phenylalanine). Serine features an aliphatic hydroxyl group (-OH) that serves as the target for phosphorylation by kinases. Hydroxyproline is formed via the post-translational modification of incorporated proline residues. Phenylalanine contains a phenyl/benzene ring, while the indole ring system belongs to tryptophan.
